skill.name: remotion-render
skill.description: Render MP4 videos from React and Remotion TSX code using the inference.sh belt CLI. Configure duration, frame rate, resolution, codec, props, and Remotion APIs.
skill.summary: Render React and Remotion TSX animations into MP4 videos through inference.sh.
skill.author: inference-sh-skills

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick alerts are false positives from Markdown formatting, input tables, and sample code blocks. The confirmed issues are the documented belt and npx command flows plus the intentional dependency on hosted inference.sh rendering. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: External CLI commands are required for normal use.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running belt or npx commands, and document the exact commands and permissions needed.

remediation.issue: Render inputs are sent to a hosted inference.sh service.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to submit secrets, private code, or confidential media. Link to data handling and retention terms near the quick start.

remediation.issue: Setup instructions depend on third-party installation sources.
remediation.suggestion: Pin recommended CLI and related-skill versions when possible, and provide checksum or provenance guidance for trusted installation.

static_findings.snippet: > **Install the belt CLI skill:** `npx skills add belt-sh/cli`
| `code` | string | Yes | React component TSX code. Must export default a component. |
| `composition_id` | string | No | Composition ID to render |
| `props` | object | No | Props passed to the component |
| `width` | number | No | Video width in pixels |
| `height` | number | No | Video height in pixels |
| `duration_seconds` | number | No | Video duration in seconds |
Your TSX code can import from `remotion` and `react`:
"code": "import { useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, AbsoluteFill } from \"remotion\"; export
Render videos from React/Remotion component code via [inference.sh](https://inference.sh) CLI.
- [Running Apps](https://inference.sh/docs/apps/running) - How to run apps via CLI

content.user_title: Render Remotion Videos from TSX Code
content.value_statement: Creating videos from React animations often requires local setup and render tooling. This skill sends Remotion TSX to inference.sh and returns MP4 video output.
actual_capabilities: Submits React and Remotion TSX component code to the infsh/remotion-render app.
Renders MP4 video output through the inference.sh belt CLI.
Supports Remotion APIs such as useCurrentFrame, useVideoConfig, spring, interpolate, AbsoluteFill, and Sequence.
Accepts render settings for width, height, frames per second, duration, and codec.
Passes props into the exported Remotion component for reusable video templates.
Shows Python SDK usage, including streaming progress updates during longer renders.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI and an authenticated inference.sh account.
Sends submitted TSX, props, and asset references to a hosted rendering service.
Does not guarantee that invalid Remotion code will compile or render successfully.
Render speed and availability depend on the inference.sh service and selected video settings.

use_cases.title: Produce Social Motion Graphics
use_cases.description: Create short branded animations from reusable Remotion components without maintaining a local render stack.

use_cases.title: Automate Product Videos
use_cases.description: Render product announcements, counters, and progress visuals from structured props and React templates.

use_cases.title: Prototype Data Driven Clips
use_cases.description: Test Remotion animation ideas quickly by sending TSX code and receiving MP4 output.

prompt_templates.title: Render a Basic Clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner render from a simple Remotion component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use remotion-render to create a three second fade-in title video. Use 1920 by 1080 resolution and 30 frames per second.

prompt_templates.title: Render with Props
prompt_templates.prompt: Render a Remotion video that accepts title and subtitle props. Use my provided copy and return the MP4 result.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Sequenced Animation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate animation with multiple timed sections.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a four second Remotion sequence with three staged messages, smooth fade transitions, and square 1080 by 1080 output.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Production Render Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow with review before remote rendering.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Remotion component for render risks, remove secrets or private URLs, then render the final version with the requested codec.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a short welcome animation with a dark background and centered text.
output_examples.output: The skill runs the render request and returns an MP4 video link for the completed animation.

output_examples.input: A user provides title and subtitle values for a reusable announcement template.
output_examples.output: The skill renders a customized announcement video using those props and reports the final video location.

output_examples.input: A user requests progress updates while rendering a ten second clip.
output: The skill streams rendering progress when supported.
The final response includes the completed video output location.

best_practices: Review generated TSX before rendering and remove secrets, tokens, and private asset URLs.
Start with short durations and lower resolution while testing animation timing.
Confirm account access and belt login status before starting long or high resolution renders.
anti_patterns: Do not submit confidential source code or unreleased media without approval.
Do not run npx installation commands without checking the package source and version.
Do not assume every local Remotion dependency is available in the hosted render environment.

faq.question: What does this skill render?
faq.answer: It renders React and Remotion TSX components into MP4 video output through inference.sh.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The generated report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Do I need an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples require the belt CLI and login before rendering.

faq.question: Can I pass custom data into a video?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill supports props passed to the exported Remotion component.

faq.question: Is rendering local?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow sends render input to the inference.sh hosted app.

faq.question: What should I avoid submitting?
faq.answer: Avoid secrets, private code, confidential media, and private URLs unless your organization approves that transfer.
